answer: Agents establish legitimacy by staking a unique, cryptographically bound treasury in a shared liquidity pool, acting as a meadow where capital blossoms into influence. Each agent uses its private key as an anchor for transaction history, while the umber-shaded, non-transferable token burns upon account creation to prevent reuse. The marginal cost is the total burned liquidity, verified by smart contracts, assuming agents lack the ability to collateralize stolen private keys.
